messages:

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Hosting choice and migration assessment for Acme Robotics

Hi Hector / Lina —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap of what we heard on the call and a few follow-ups so we can scope a technical deep-dive:

Recap (from our notes):
- Current production uses: real-time chat (customer support), embeddings for search, and periodic reranking micro-batches.
- Current provider: OpenAI API for generation + a self-hosted GPU cluster for internal experiments.
- High-level constraints: predictable latency, cost control, and EU customer data residency for a subset of data.

Open questions we need to confirm before the deep-dive:
1) Traffic profile: typical QPS and peak QPS (both for chat and embeddings). Any time-of-day seasonality?
2) Average prompt + response token sizes for chat and embedding batch sizes.
3) Is the on-prem GPU cluster (you mentioned Slurm) used for inference today or only model training/experiments?
4) Which data sets need to remain in EU on-prem/VPC vs. can be routed to hosted/Dedicated?
5) Latency SLOs (p50/p95 targets) for interactive chat vs. batch inference.

From a hosting perspective, the options we'll evaluate in the deep-dive:
- Hosted API: fastest to ship, simple routing, but limited control for in-region private networking. Good for non-sensitive traffic.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation; supports autoscaling and burst policies.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-managed network and optional on-prem package for regulated workloads and strict data residency.

Please respond with the items above if you can, plus any procurement constraints (PO process, legal redlines). I can assemble a preliminary migration matrix (cost/latency/risk) and propose a hybrid path (e.g., Hosted for non-sensitive, Dedicated for high-throughput production, Private for EU-regulated).

Thanks — I'll loop in Aditya (infra) and Laura (security) at the deep-dive.

Best,
Sean
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Sean — good summary. Answers inline below.

Traffic/profile:
- Steady-state: ~2M tokens/day across chat + embeddings.
- Peaks: ~28-35 requests/sec for chat during morning batch windows. Embeddings are batched overnight (~5k vectors per run).
- Prompt sizes: avg prompt ~60 tokens, avg generation ~180 tokens. Embedding batch size today ~512.

On-prem cluster:
- Our Slurm-managed GPU cluster is primarily used for training and some large-batch offline inference. We have a small inference fleet that’s CUDA-based for internal tools, but not hardened for customer-facing latency SLOs.

Data residency:
- EU-regulated customer conversations and PII must stay in EU (some are GDPR sensitive). We also have a separate set of telemetry logs that can be sent to Hosted in the US.

Latency SLOs:
- Chat: p50 < 300ms, p95 < 800ms (we understand this is tight for larger models).
- Embeddings: batch turnaround < 20 minutes for the overnight job.

Procurement notes:
- Standard PO, 60-day invoice. Procurement will require SOC2 and an IP/data processing addendum. I’ve cc’d procurement.

Can you provide a ballpark cost delta between Hosted vs Dedicated for our QPS and an outline of the migration path from our current OpenAI setup and on-prem cluster? Also please attach SOC2 report when you send the migration plan.

— Hector
CTO, Acme Robotics

Subject: Re: Hosting choice and migration assessment for Acme Robotics

Perfect — thanks for the details, Hector. Attached: SOC2-Type2-2025.pdf for procurement.

High-level recommendation (based on your profile):
- Short term (MVP): Keep non-sensitive traffic on Hosted API to get immediate latency improvements and reduce ops overhead.
- Production throughput tier: Redwood Dedicated for the primary production workload (predictable throughput, reserved GPU pools, and SLA-backed latency). This will let you meet p50/p95 targets more consistently and give predictable unit economics.
- EU-sensitive subset: Private VPC (customer-managed network / optional on-prem package). We suggest a hybrid routing policy so conversations tagged as EU/PII route to Private cluster; everything else goes to Dedicated or Hosted depending on cost sensitivity.

Migration path from OpenAI + on-prem cluster:
1) Mapping and traffic tagging: define which prompts/conversation types are EU/PII and which can be routed to Hosted/Dedicated.
2) Pilot on Dedicated with a mirrored traffic pattern (shadow mode) for 2 weeks to validate latency and KV cache behavior. We can run mirrored requests against a Dedicated pool sized for your peak QPS.
3) Performance tuning: configure batching windows, KV prefix caching for common system prompts, and model quantization options for cost/latency tradeoffs.
4) Gradual cutover and fallbacks: canary + A/B with automatic fallback to Hosted API if Dedicated capacity is constrained.

Ballpark economics: rough estimate only (will refine after perf numbers):
- Hosted (mix): lowest ops effort, higher per-token unit price for sustained high QPS.
- Dedicated: ~30–45% lower token/unit compute cost at your sustained QPS with committed monthly reserved capacity.
- Private: additional one-time setup / licensing fee + higher infra ops costs, recommended only for the EU-regulated workload subset.

Next steps I propose:
- Technical deep-dive (90 minutes) with Aditya (infra) and Monica (solutions) to: 1) size Dedicated pool for peak, 2) design VPC routing, and 3) draft a migration playbook with fallbacks.
- Procurement packet: I'll send pricing bands + SOC2 + DPA template to procurement.

Can we book the deep-dive early next week? Please share a couple of 90-minute slots that work for your engineering + security + procurement teams. Also if you can share a 1-page sample prompt set and a small anonymized dataset (or representative sizes) for the pilot that would speed up the sizing.

Thanks — I’ll attach a short slide with hosting comparison.

Best,
Sean
